answers.rationale: The stated tradeoffs do not justify a blanket open-jaw or round-trip rule; the comparison policy explicitly accounts for fee, connection, cargo, and backtracking.
The suitable policy is to compare the round trip with the open-jaw using drop fee, total travel time, and connection risk rather than defaulting to either airport.
The choice supplies material competing factors—backtracking, SUV drop fee, boxes, roads, and reimbursable driving—so the explicit three-way comparison policy is uniquely appropriate.
The Monday flight reaches the hotel roughly three hours before an informal 2:00 prep, while Sunday adds substantial cost; Sunday becomes warranted only if the obligation changes.
A 7:05 arrival plus a 45- to 60-minute transfer cannot reliably support mandatory 8:15 roll call, and the pre-night is approved.
The Saturday nonstop plus a short hotel-to-venue transfer leaves several hours before a no-setup 4:00 ceremony; the prior-night options add unjustified cost or disruption.
The itinerary is walkable, airport rideshare is simple, parking is costly, and there is only one short off-site trip with no boxes to transport.
Multiple campus stops, brochure boxes, included hotel parking, and transfer-heavy transit make a rental appropriate, without imposing an unconditional rental rule.
Sessions are accessible by walking or transit, parking is expensive, cargo is minimal, and rideshare addresses the airport, rain, and Seaport dinner.
The nearby STS departure follows the meeting with a workable 1-hour-45-minute connection and avoids a long drive; its use is appropriately conditioned on fare and connection viability.
The BFF itinerary has a very short connection and no recovery option, whereas the post-visit drive still leaves ample time for the later DEN nonstop.
ITH is near the final visit and offers a workable 90-minute connection; the much longer JFK drive is not justified solely by a nonstop when fares are comparable.
With no car, an 8:00 start, and a 9:30 reception, the official walkable hotel has clear schedule and access advantages that outweigh breakfast and suburban savings.
The suburban Chandler or Tempe location is near the early school visits and provides breakfast and free parking; downtown adds valet cost without itinerary benefit.
A downtown hotel supports the convention-center sessions, late downtown dinner, car-free travel, and early King Street departure better than airport or Bellevue lodging.
